memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If a malicious witness takes the stand to accuse someone of a crime, the two people involved in the dispute must stand in the presence of the Lord before the priests and the judges who are in office at the time. The judges must make a thorough investigation, and if the witness proves to be a liar, giving false testimony against a fellow Israelite, then do to the false witness as that witness intended to do to the other party. You must purge the evil from among you. - Deut 19:16-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God addresses the danger of a malicious witness, someone who lies to bring harm on another. Such a case was to be investigated thoroughly before God, and if the witness was proven to be a liar, the very punishment he intended for his victim would fall on him instead. God took false accusation with utmost seriousness, because a lie in court could destroy an innocent person's life.

Notice the phrase "in the presence of the Lord." Justice was to be conducted as before God Himself, who sees all things and cannot be deceived. A liar might fool a human judge, but never God. And the thorough investigation guarded against both false accusers and hasty verdicts.

God's hatred of false testimony flows from His own nature, for He is the God of truth who cannot lie. Bearing false witness is so serious that it made God's list of ten great commands (Exod 20:16). Our words have power to protect or to destroy. God calls His people to be people of truth in every setting, refusing to twist facts or bear false witness against anyone. In a culture where reputations are damaged carelessly online and off, how carefully do you guard the truth in what you say about others?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How carefully do you guard the truth about others?
2. Where might your words have damaged someone unfairly?
3. What would speaking as "before the Lord" change for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are the God of truth. Guard my lips from falsehood, and help me speak truthfully and fairly about everyone. Amen.
